h1: The 8 Best Bluegill Crankbaits of 2026 for Bass and Panfish Water, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 bluegill pattern crankbaits scored on running depth, hook size, weight, action and value, from squarebills to lipless baits.
summary: The Strike King KVD 1.5 Squarebill in bluegill is the all-round pick for 3 to 5 feet of water. The Lucky Craft LC 1.5 is the premium squarebill for clear water, the KVD 2.5 Shallow runs just 10 inches deep for brush and rock, and the Rapala Dives-To reaches 6 feet. The TRUSCEND is a bargain only for occasional use.
intro: A bluegill crankbait is usually not meant to catch bluegill. It is a bass lure painted to look like the fish bass eat most in spring and summer, and the colour is the least important decision you will make about it. The part that decides whether you catch anything is running depth, because a lure that tracks above or below the fish is just a swimming ornament.

We ranked eight bluegill pattern crankbaits by the numbers on the listings: stated dive depth, weight, hook size, body style and construction. Shallow squarebills dominate because most bluegill-eating bass sit near cover in a few feet of water, so we sorted by how well each lure covers a specific depth band, not by hype.

products.name: Strike King KVD 1.5 Squarebill Fishing Lure, Bluegill | 3/8-Ounce
products.verdict: The best all-round squarebill for a 3 to 5 foot band, with size 3 trebles.
products.description:
The KVD 1.5 is a 3/8 ounce squarebill that dives 3 to 5 feet, fitted with size 3 treble hooks. It has chip-resistant finishes, 3D eyes and a hunting action that wanders instead of tracking perfectly straight, which is the quality that triggers reaction strikes off rock, stumps and dock pilings.

It takes first place because that 3 to 5 foot band is where the most bass sit around cover in warm months, and 3/8 ounce casts well on a baitcaster. It beats the KVD 1.0 below when you need more depth and a bigger profile, and it beats the Rapala when you want deflection off cover, because a squarebill bill bounces where a round lip digs in.

Buy it as the first bluegill crankbait in the box. The caveat is that deeper than 5 feet it simply stops reaching fish, so it is not for open mid-depth structure.
products.idealFor: Anglers fishing docks, rock and wood in a few feet of water.
products.skipIf: You fish open water deeper than 5 feet.

products.name: LUCKY CRAFT LC 1.5 Silent Squarebill Crankbait Fishing Lure, 2-3/8"
products.verdict: A quiet, floating 1/2 ounce squarebill for pressured water, ranked just behind the Strike King on value.
products.description:
The LC 1.5 is a 2-3/8 inch, 1/2 ounce floating squarebill that dives to about 4 feet. It is built from high-float plastic and is described as having a tight wobble, strong deflection off cover and true tracking on both steady and stop-and-go retrieves.

It lands second because it is heavier than the KVD 1.5, which helps casting distance into wind, and the silent body suits clear, pressured water where rattles can spook fish. It is behind the Strike King because it covers a narrower depth band, with one stated figure of 4 feet, and it sits in the same under $30 bucket as the rest without adding a clear performance gain over the leader.

It suits anglers on clear lakes who have noticed rattle baits losing effectiveness. The listing does not specify hook size, so check before you swap hooks.
products.idealFor: Clear-water anglers fishing pressured shallow cover.
products.skipIf: You want a rattle to call fish in stained water.

products.name: Strike King KVD 2.5 Shallow Fishing Lure, Natural Bream | Shallow Running Squarebill Crankbait, 3/8-Ounce
products.verdict: Runs only 10 inches deep, so it fishes water the other squarebills dig through.
products.description:
This 3/8 ounce squarebill runs about 10 inches deep, with size 3 black nickel treble hooks and a design meant to deflect off rocks in extremely shallow water. The finish is Natural Bream, a softer pattern than the bright bluegill colours.

It ranks third because it is a specialist. At 10 inches it can fish over grass tops, shallow flats and spawn bank rubble where a 3 to 5 foot diver would foul on every cast. The tradeoff against the KVD 1.5 is simple: it solves one problem very well and cannot reach deeper fish at all. The black nickel hooks are a small upgrade for saltwater-adjacent corrosion.

Buy it for early spring and post-spawn bank fishing. Note that the listing text uses both 2.5 and 2.25 for the model name, so check the pack before ordering.
products.idealFor: Shallow flats, grass tops and spawn banks.
products.skipIf: You fish most of your day past 3 feet.

products.name: Rapala Dives-To Crankbait, Diving Hard Bait Lure, 2", Bluegill
products.verdict: The only pick here rated to 6 feet, and a good choice from shore or a kayak.
products.description:
The Dives-To is a 2 inch, 3/8 ounce diving crankbait rated to run about 6 feet, carrying two number 5 hooks. It uses a round lip for a consistent diving line, and the listing pitches it for casting from shore, a boat or a kayak for bass and walleye.

It ranks fourth because that 6 foot depth reaches fish the squarebills cannot, but the round lip digs in and snags where a squarebill would bounce. Against the KVD 1.5 you gain 1 to 3 feet of depth and lose cover deflection. With only two hooks it also gives you fewer chances to stay hooked than a three-hook rig.

Buy it for open points, weed edges and deeper docks. Keep it away from heavy timber, where the lip will hang up.
products.idealFor: Points, weed edges and deeper docks.
products.skipIf: You fish dense wood or rock.

products.name: Strike King KVD 1.0 Squarebill Fishing Lure, Neon Bluegill | 1/4-Ounce
products.verdict: A 1/4 ounce squarebill for 2 to 4 feet, ideal when bass are fussy or the water is cold.
products.description:
The KVD 1.0 is a 1/4 ounce squarebill that dives 2 to 4 feet and carries size 5 treble hooks. It has the same chip-resistant finish, 3D eyes and wandering action as the 1.5, in a smaller body and in the brighter Neon Bluegill pattern.

It ranks fifth because the smaller body fits cold water, pressured fish and light baitcasting gear, where the 1.5 can feel too large. The size 5 hooks are smaller, though, which means fewer fish stay pinned on a head shake. Compared with the 1.5 you give up a foot of depth and some casting distance, so it is a niche pick.

Choose it when bass are following a bigger bait without eating. Do not make it your only squarebill.
products.skipIf: You need distance or deeper depth.

products.name: Strike King Red Eyed Shad Fishing Lure, Lipless Crankbait, Bluegill | 1/2-Ounce
products.verdict: A sinking lipless bait for covering grass and open flats, with free-floating rattles.
products.description:
The Red Eyed Shad is a 1/2 ounce lipless crankbait with 3D eyes, free-floating rattles and size 3 treble hooks. With no lip it sinks, so you pick the depth by counting the lure down, and the listing recommends an erratic lift-and-drop retrieve to trigger strikes on the fall.

It ranks sixth because it solves a different problem from the squarebills. It lets you cover open water and grass quickly, but it has no built-in depth and no cover deflection, so you manage both with your rod and reel. The 1/2 ounce weight casts well, though it can snag grass without care.

Buy it if you fish grass lines or open flats and want sound and vibration. Skip it if you want a lure that tracks on its own.
pros: Casts a long way at 1/2 oz
Works over grass and open flats
products.skipIf: You want a lure that tracks on its own.

products.name: Berkley Frittside Fishing Hard Bait, HD Bluegill, 2 1/4in (1/3 oz)
products.verdict: A flat-sided crankbait with a FlashDisc, built to throw the most flash in the Berkley range.
products.description:
The Frittside is a 2 1/4 inch, 1/3 ounce hard bait with a flat side profile described as producing the most flash of any Berkley crankbait. A FlashDisc improves tracking, and the listing claims a tight, balsa-like thumping action.

It ranks seventh because the listing gives no running depth for this size, which is the number that matters most. Larger models in the series are noted as weighted-bill versions for diving deeper, so you must choose the size to match your target depth. Against the Rapala you gain flash but lose a stated depth.

Choose it when water is stained and flash helps fish find the bait. Confirm the model size before ordering, since the listing covers several.
cons: No depth figure for this size
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed running depth.

products.name: TRUSCEND Crankbaits Fishing Lures Hard Swimbait for Bass Trout Crappie Crank Baits Freshwater and Saltwater
products.verdict: A low-cost ABS squarebill with a steel rattle, limited to depths under two feet.
products.description:
The TRUSCEND is a squarebill built from ABS with a stainless steel ball rattle and number 6 high carbon treble hooks. It is rated to run from 0 to 1.6 feet, which makes it a very shallow bait for bass, perch, trout and crappie.

It finishes last because the listing is the least specific about weight and the depth band is the narrowest here. It does cost less than the name-brand squarebills and carries a rattle, which helps in stained water, but the finish and hooks are unknown quantities beside the Strike King.

Buy it to fill a tackle tray cheaply, or as a lure you will not mind losing in snags. Replace the hooks if you intend to chase bigger fish.
products.idealFor: Filling a tackle tray on a budget.
products.skipIf: You want proven finish and hooks.

methodology.title: Running depth
methodology.description: We ranked lures by the clarity and usefulness of their stated dive depth, since a lure at the wrong depth catches nothing.

methodology.title: Body style and cover handling
methodology.description: We compared squarebill, round-lip and lipless designs for how they behave on rock, wood and grass.

methodology.title: Weight and casting
methodology.description: We read listed ounces and length to judge how each lure casts on baitcasting and spinning gear.

methodology.title: Hooks and hardware
methodology.description: We favoured named hook sizes and finishes, and marked any listing that leaves them out.

methodology.title: Pattern and value
methodology.description: We judged the bluegill finish for realism and chip resistance, then weighed it against the price bucket.

whatMatters.detail: Running depth is how far below the surface the lure dives on a standard retrieve. Bass hold in specific bands, so a lure that runs 10 inches deep will not reach a fish at 5 feet. Check the listed range, such as 3 to 5 feet on the KVD 1.5, and match it to the water you fish.

A squarebill deflects off cover and keeps fishing, while a round lip digs deeper and tracks straighter but can snag. A lipless bait sinks and relies on your retrieve. Pick squarebills for rock and wood, round lips for open water, and lipless for grass flats.

Treble hook size sets how well a lure holds fish and how often it snags. Size 3 hooks, on the KVD 1.5, hold bigger bass than size 5, on the KVD 1.0. Look for a stated size on the listing and be ready to upgrade cheap hooks.

A rattle adds sound and helps in stained or windy water, while a silent body suits clear, pressured fish. The Red Eyed Shad and TRUSCEND rattle, and the Lucky Craft is silent. Choose by water clarity, not habit.

Weight controls casting distance and how the lure feels on the rod. The 1/4 ounce KVD 1.0 suits lighter gear, while the 1/2 ounce Lucky Craft and Red Eyed Shad cast farther into wind. Match the weight to your rod's rated lure range.

howToChoose.intro: Depth is the one number that must match the water in front of you.

cards.label: Squarebill
cards.text: It floats, dives to a set depth and deflects off cover. Best on rock, wood and docks. Picks: Strike King KVD 1.5, KVD 1.0, KVD 2.5, Lucky Craft LC 1.5.

cards.label: Lipless
cards.text: It sinks, you control the depth, and it covers water fast. Best on grass and open flats. Pick: Strike King Red Eyed Shad.

howToChoose.note: Start with a squarebill unless you are fishing grass flats.

howToChoose.subheading: For Shore and Kayak Fishing Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A compact lure that casts well, a stated running depth and sharp hooks, since you cannot chase fish with a motor.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Rapala Dives-To is pitched for shore, boat and kayak, and the KVD 1.0 suits light gear from the bank.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You fish pressured water often. The Lucky Craft LC 1.5 and Strike King models offer better finishes and stated hook sizes.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You fish snaggy cover. The TRUSCEND is cheap enough to lose, and you can upgrade the hooks.

faq.a: Mostly they catch bass, which feed on bluegill. The bluegill pattern is a colour, not a target species. Panfish may hit the smaller KVD 1.0, but it is designed for bass.

faq.q: What line should I use with these crankbaits?
faq.a: Strike King recommends baitcasting tackle with fluorocarbon line for the KVD and Red Eyed Shad lures. Fluorocarbon sinks, so it helps squarebills dive and keeps the hooking angle clean.

faq.q: Is a premium crankbait worth it over a cheap one?
faq.a: Often yes. The Lucky Craft and Strike King offer stated hook sizes, floating bodies and chip-resistant finishes. The TRUSCEND is acceptable for casual use, but plan to swap its hooks.

faq.q: How do I get the most depth from a squarebill?
faq.a: Use a lighter line, point the rod tip down and reel quickly. The KVD 1.5 tops out near 5 feet, so heavier line will cut that figure. If you need more depth, switch to the Rapala Dives-To.

faq.q: How should I maintain crankbait hooks?
faq.a: Check points after every snag and replace dull trebles. The KVD 2.5 Shallow comes with black nickel hooks, which resist corrosion, but all trebles dull on rock. Rinse any lure used in salt.

faq.q: Can I use these in saltwater?
faq.a: The TRUSCEND listing claims freshwater and saltwater use, while the KVD 2.5 has black nickel hooks. For most others, assume freshwater only and rinse with fresh water if you do take them to brackish waters.

finalTake: The Strike King KVD 1.5 is the bluegill crankbait to buy first, because it covers the 3 to 5 foot band where most bass feed around cover. Add the KVD 2.5 Shallow for banks and flats, the Rapala Dives-To for 6 feet, and the Lucky Craft when the water is clear. The Red Eyed Shad and Frittside are specialists, and the TRUSCEND is a cheap extra. Match depth first, colour second.
